scenario.summary: Attackers exploit Windows Volume Shadow Copy (VSS) for both credential theft and ransomware protection. By creating shadow copies, they can perform offline extraction of sensitive files like the Active Directory database (ntds.dit), and by deleting them, they prevent victims from using local snapshots to recover from ransomware encryption.

hunt.name: VSS Manipulation and Data Impact
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the abuse of the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) by correlating the execution of administrative tools with downstream high-impact file activity. It first identifies the use of vssadmin, ntdsutil, and wmic for shadow copy manipulation and then corroborates these leads by checking for ntds.dit extraction or mass file modifications. By scoping to Windows assets and constraining corroboration to high-signal hosts, the hunt minimizes noise from legitimate backup agents and RMM scripts while ensuring high-performance execution across large fleets.

config.scoping_notes: Start with Domain Controllers and high-value File Servers. Populate 'scoping_hosts' with the identified Windows systems to focus subsequent analysis.
config.beyond_detection: A single rule on shadow deletion is too noisy due to legitimate IT maintenance. This hunt pivots to prevalence and corroborates with targeted file telemetry to reduce false positives.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%windows%') AND collected_at >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Focus the hunt on Windows hosts that likely contain VSS capabilities or critical data targets.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames running Windows. Silence indicates no Windows hosts are monitored.

primitive_config.label: Identify Windows Assets
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%windows%') AND collected_at >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames running Windows. Silence indicates no Windows hosts are monitored.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) IN ('vssadmin.exe', 'wmic.exe', 'powershell.exe', 'ntdsutil.exe')) AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%shadow%' AND (instr(',' || '{{scoping_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0 OR '{{scoping_hosts}}' = '') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the use of vssadmin, ntdsutil, wmic, or powershell to create or delete shadow copies on the identified Windows assets.
config.expected_signal: Command lines explicitly manipulating shadow copies. Presence on non-backup servers is highly suspicious.

primitive_config.label: VSS Manipulation Commands
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) IN ('vssadmin.exe', 'wmic.exe', 'powershell.exe', 'ntdsutil.exe')) AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%shadow%' AND (instr(',' || '{{scoping_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0 OR '{{scoping_hosts}}' = '') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Command lines explicitly manipulating shadow copies. Presence on non-backup servers is highly suspicious.

config.content: SELECT parent_process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%vssadmin.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY parent_process_name HAVING host_count <= 2
config.description: Identify unusual initiators of vssadmin.exe that do not match known backup or RMM agent patterns.
config.expected_signal: A parent process seen on only one or two hosts; suggests a manual command or non-standard tool.

primitive_config.label: Rare VSS Parent Processes
primitive_config.content: SELECT parent_process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%vssadmin.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY parent_process_name HAVING host_count <= 2
primitive_config.expected: A parent process seen on only one or two hosts; suggests a manual command or non-standard tool.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, file_path, activity_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%ntds.dit' AND instr(',' || '{{vss_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify processes interacting with the Active Directory database on hosts where VSS manipulation was already observed.
config.expected_signal: Processes touching the AD database. High-confidence sign of credential theft when paired with VSS creation.

primitive_config.label: Access to NTDS.dit
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, file_path, activity_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%ntds.dit' AND instr(',' || '{{vss_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Processes touching the AD database. High-confidence sign of credential theft when paired with VSS creation.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, activity_name, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (activity_id IN (3, 4, 5)) AND instr(',' || '{{vss_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, activity_name HAVING touches >= {{file_touch_threshold}}
config.description: Identify targeted hosts experiencing high rates of file updates or deletions, which suggests ransomware encryption follow-on.
config.expected_signal: A significant volume of file touches on a suspicious host. Zero results proof nothing without host-level visibility.

primitive_config.label: Mass File Modification Count
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, activity_name, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (activity_id IN (3, 4, 5)) AND instr(',' || '{{vss_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, activity_name HAVING touches >= {{file_touch_threshold}}
